claim: On your site, a visitor who types "tee" can land on your T-shirt page first, because you set that on the Search settings page (a promoted result is shown on page one ahead of organic results, or a synonym widens the search).
Synonyms, typo fixes and promoted results are all set on the Search settings page.
The search button sits in the site header and opens a box that shows matching pages as the visitor types.
A results page lists matching pages with the matching words highlighted in the title and excerpt.
The header button appears only if the theme uses the header from the Navigation package (the render hook targets capell-navigation::components.header.navigation).
Turning off Enable search makes search disappear from the site altogether: it hides the header button and answers 404 on the search page, type-ahead and click-tracking routes.

Search reads the list of public pages that Discovery Foundation keeps, so there is no separate search index to build (default driver site_discovery; the list itself is built by Discovery Foundation's BuildPublicUrlRegistryAction in the discovery-foundation package).
An edit shows on the next search: page, URL, translation, site, domain and language saves or deletes flush the cached page list after commit.

It matches the title, the address and the first 1000 characters of page text as lowercase plain text, so text further down a long page is not found (the 1000-character limit is BODY_TEXT_LIMIT in Discovery Foundation's DiscoverPublicPagesAction, in the discovery-foundation package).
Administrators get top, trending and zero-result searches on the admin dashboard (widgets gated to admin and super_admin roles).
The dashboard figures are all taken from the results page, which is the only place searches are recorded.
The dashboard shows what people looked for and did not find (zero-result searches).
